thread:
Ritesh K: quick q — when SCIM removes a user, does our logging pipeline redact emails/PII for past requests? I'm seeing a few auth logs with user_email in request_body. cc @Mel S

scim-bot: 🔔 SCIM event processed: user.delete id=u-9843 timestamp=2024-11-10T15:23:11Z

Mel S: we don't retroactively redact by default — logs are immutable for 90d retention. we do scrub tokens with regex on ingest but email addresses slip through in request bodies :/

Alex P: policy says PII should be hashed at ingest. looks like the scim-delete handler doesn't trigger the downstream redact job. I'll file ACTION-452 to attach to infra backlog.

Ritesh K: thanks. can we do a safe-delete for the user in question (u-9843)? legal requested removal of identifiable data.

Mel S: for safe-delete we need an access-approval ticket and infra exec sign-off. tagging @Alex P to own approval flow.

Alex P: will open ticket and ping legal. also quick Q on SCIM group -> RBAC mapping: where's the canonical mapping? I remember a yaml somewhere.

Mel S: mapping lives in infra/config/scim_mapper.yml in the infra repo. snippet:
```
groups:
  engineering: eng-role
  data-science: ds-role
  admins: admin-role
```

Mel S: update via PR, then deploy to scim-sync service.

Ritesh K: perfect. can someone add a check so when scim-delete happens we enqueue redact task? :eyes:

Alex P: yep will include in ACTION-452. estimate: small PR + cron sweep over historical logs for affected user ids. i'll try to get this in this sprint.

Mel S: FYI I've added a temporary workaround to filter emails from request_body in the ingest lambda; not perfect but reduces exposure. :thumbsup:

Ritesh K: awesome — thanks both. filing follow-ups in #incidents for tracking.
